name: FL-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Wasserman Schultz's large financial advantage ($1.9M cash vs ~$41K)
No polling and no expert ratings, but fundamentals strongly favor Democrats
model.rationale: The seat's +20 Democratic lean, Wasserman Schultz's incumbency and overwhelming fundraising edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 95% all point to a Safe Democratic hold. The Republican has raised only about $64,000, leaving no realistic path to close a two-dozen-point structural gap.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D) is running.

overview:
Debbie Wasserman Schultz, a well-established incumbent, is heavily favored to hold this South Florida seat for Democrats following Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick's resignation. The district leans Democratic by about 20 points, giving Republicans a steep structural disadvantage in any general election.

The financial picture is lopsided: Wasserman Schultz has raised over $3.3 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Republican Brent Andersen has raised roughly $64,000. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 95% chance of winning. With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic victory in the mid-20s margin range.
